title: CT Slice Volume Viewer
prompt:
Create a 3D CT-style volume slice viewer using Three.js with procedurally generated volume data. The entire application must be in a single HTML file.

## Three.js Import
Use this importmap in <head>:
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>
Then in <script type="module">:
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';

## Scene Setup
- Background 0x000000.
- PerspectiveCamera at (0, 0, 30), looking at origin.
- OrbitControls enabled.
- Ambient light (0x808080).

## Procedural Volume Data
- Generate a 64x64x64 voxel grid.
- The volume contains a sphere of radius 20 (centered) with smooth falloff, plus 3 smaller dense spheres inside (radius 5 each, at random offsets) simulating organs/lesions.
- Add Perlin-like noise: for each voxel, add sin(x*0.3)*cos(y*0.4)*sin(z*0.5) * 30 to create texture variation.
- Voxel values range 0-255 (uint8).

## Slice Visualization
- Display three orthogonal slice planes (axial/XZ, coronal/XY, sagittal/YZ).
- Each slice is a PlaneGeometry textured with a DataTexture created from the corresponding 2D slice of the volume.
- Apply a window/level mapping: pixel_display = clamp((voxel_value - (level - window/2)) / window * 255, 0, 255). Default window=200, level=128.

## Controls
- Slider (id='slider-axial', range 0 to 63, default 32) to scroll through axial slices.
- Slider (id='slider-coronal', range 0 to 63, default 32) to scroll through coronal slices.
- Slider (id='slider-sagittal', range 0 to 63, default 32) to scroll through sagittal slices.
- Slider (id='slider-window', range 1 to 400, default 200) for window width.
- Slider (id='slider-level', range 0 to 255, default 128) for window level.
- Press 'R' to reset all sliders to defaults.
- Checkbox (id='check-axial') to toggle axial plane visibility (default checked).
- Checkbox (id='check-coronal') to toggle coronal plane visibility (default checked).
- Checkbox (id='check-sagittal') to toggle sagittal plane visibility (default checked).

## Crosshair
- Draw thin colored lines at the intersection of the three planes: red for axial, green for coronal, blue for sagittal.

## HUD (id='hud')
- Axial slice index (id='hud-axial')
- Coronal slice index (id='hud-coronal')
- Sagittal slice index (id='hud-sagittal')
- Window value (id='hud-window')
- Level value (id='hud-level')
- Voxel value at crosshair intersection (id='hud-voxel'): the value at (sagittal, axial, coronal) indices

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ updated every frame:
- `axialSlice`: number (current axial index)
- `coronalSlice`: number (current coronal index)
- `sagittalSlice`: number (current sagittal index)
- `windowWidth`: number
- `windowLevel`: number
- `voxelAtCrosshair`: number (0-255)
- `axialVisible`: boolean
- `coronalVisible`: boolean
- `sagittalVisible`: boolean
- `volumeSize`: number (always 64)
- `frameCount`: number
- `isReset`: boolean (true when all defaults)

Ensure the animation loop updates __3D_STATE__ every frame before rendering.
physics_constraints: Slice indices must be clamped to [0, 63]. Window must be >= 1. Voxel values must be in [0, 255]. Crosshair voxel value must match the actual volume data at the intersection point. Changing slice index must update the displayed texture. Window/level must affect pixel brightness mapping.
